title: The sharp spot behind your right shoulder blade
intro: Five moves that open the space between your spine and shoulder blade, then breathe into it. Breathing into that space often lets a cranky rib joint or muscle settle.
howToUse: Do one round of all five, then take a deep breath to test. If one clearly helps, do that one a few more times through the day.
guideline: A stretch, or tenderness you can live with, is fine. If a move brings back the sharp catch, skip it.

exercises.name: Across-body reach
exercises.forWhat: Slides the shoulder blade away from your spine. Often the quickest to help.
steps: Sit or stand. Reach your right hand across and hold a doorframe on your left, at chest height.
Let your body weight pull back so the right shoulder blade slides away from your spine.
Round your upper back a little.
Take 5 slow, deep breaths into the sore spot.

exercises.name: Child's pose, side reach
exercises.forWhat: Stretches down the right side of your back while you breathe.
steps: Kneel and sit back onto your heels, folding forward.
Walk both hands over to the left until you feel a stretch down the right side of your back.
Breathe deep into your right back ribs, 5 to 8 times.

exercises.name: Thread the needle
exercises.forWhat: Twists the upper back and opens the shoulder blade.
steps: Start on your hands and knees.
Slide your right arm under your body toward the left, lowering your right shoulder and the side of your head toward the floor.
Stay for 5 breaths, then come back.

exercises.name: Open book
exercises.forWhat: Gently turns the upper back while you lie on your side.
steps: Lie on your left side, knees bent and stacked, both arms straight out in front.
Open your right arm up and over toward the floor behind you. Follow it with your eyes.
Go only as far as feels okay, then come back.

exercises.name: Ball release
exercises.forWhat: Presses gently on the sore spot while you breathe.
exercises.needs: A tennis ball and a wall
steps: Put a tennis ball between a wall and the sore spot.
Hug your arms across your chest. That slides the shoulder blade out of the way so the ball can reach the spot.
Lean in with steady pressure and take 3 or 4 deep breaths. Small movements are fine; don't grind on it.

avoid.title: Avoid for now
items: Crunches, sit-ups and heavy ab work. A plank may be fine because it keeps your back straight, but stop if it brings the pain on.
Sitting straight up out of bed. Roll onto your side, let your legs drop off the edge, and push up with your arms.
Sleeping in a way that presses on or pulls the right shoulder blade. Try your back, or your left side hugging a pillow. Fixing or padding the bed that started it helps too.

watchFor.title: Watch for
watchFor.lead: Get seen soon if any of these show up:
items: You're short of breath, your heart is racing, or you feel lightheaded
A calf is swollen and sore
The pain spreads, stays the same however you sit or lie, or comes with feeling sick or a sore belly
watchFor.later: Most of the time this eases in a few days and is gone in a week or two. If breathing in is still sharp after about a week, a physiotherapist can check it and often sorts a stuck rib joint in one or two visits.

check.prompt: Take a deep breath. Better, same, or worse?
check.better: Good. Which one helped most? Do that one a few more times through the day.
check.same: That's okay. It often takes a few days to ease. Try the round again later, and keep taking a few slow, deep breaths each hour, even if they catch a little.
check.worse: Skip anything that brought back the sharp catch, and go easy for today. If breathing itself is getting harder, don't wait on it.
